html:
Alexander Dubček was a Slovak communist politician, born in 1921 in Uhrovec, who led Czechoslovakia in 1968 and gave his name to "socialism with a human face".

He grew up partly in the Soviet Union and fought in the Slovak National Uprising. In January 1968 he became head of the Communist Party and let censorship lapse and debate open, the Prague Spring. In August the Warsaw Pact invaded. Dubček was taken to Moscow, forced to back down, and in 1969 removed. He worked as a forestry clerk for two decades. In 1989 he spoke to the crowds of the Velvet Revolution and became speaker of parliament. He died after a car crash in 1992.
